title: How stolen crypto is traced and frozen, and why thieves dump stablecoins fast
dek: Every blockchain transfer is public, so investigators can follow stolen funds hop by hop. Money can be stopped in two places: stablecoin issuers like Tether and Circle can freeze tokens on-chain, and exchanges can lock accounts when stolen funds arrive.

title: Kalshi prices a Democratic sweep at a record 70%. Did a fake pollster move the odds?
dek: Two days before the November 3 vote, Kalshi's market priced Democrats winning both chambers at 70%, up more than 9 points in a month. Ten days earlier, Kalshi had to explain why a fabricated pollster barely moved its election markets.

title: Seed phrase and hardware wallet safety: the words that guard your crypto
dek: Your seed phrase is the master key to your wallet: anyone who sees it can take everything, and if you lose it, nobody can restore it. A hardware wallet keeps keys offline, but only if the phrase stays offline too and the device is genuine.

title: Japan crypto rules explained: FSA registration, 95% cold storage and 2x leverage
dek: Crypto exchanges in Japan must register with the Financial Services Agency under the Payment Services Act, keep at least 95% of customer coins offline, and cap retail leverage at 2x. A 2026 government bill would revise the rules again, borrowing from securities law.

title: Bored Apes are down 96% from their record. Which NFT blue chip fell least?
dek: Most of the famous NFT collections now sit about 90% to 99% below their peak floor prices in ETH, and the marketplaces are closing. CryptoPunks are the exception, at about 76% down.

title: South Korea crypto rules explained: cold wallets, bank-held cash and jail terms
dek: Crypto exchanges in South Korea must register with the Financial Intelligence Unit and, since July 19, 2024, follow the Virtual Asset User Protection Act: customer cash held at banks, most coins in cold wallets, and prison terms for market manipulation.

title: How to check and revoke token approvals before an old one drains your wallet
dek: Look up your wallet address in an approval checker such as Etherscan's Token Approvals page or Revoke.cash, find spenders you no longer use or do not recognize, and revoke them. Each revoke is an on-chain transaction, so it costs a small network fee.

title: One address, two exchange hacks: DeepSea traces where this fall's stolen crypto went
dek: DeepSea says funds from the Bitget and Binance thefts landed at the same address. Its tracker also shows how little of the loot has reached exchanges, and how much is simply sitting still.

title: Prediction markets explained: how Kalshi and Polymarket work, and the real risks
dek: A prediction market lets people trade contracts that pay $1 if an event happens and $0 if it does not, so prices read like odds. Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated US exchange; most Polymarket markets settle on chain through the UMA oracle.

title: Singapore crypto rules explained: who needs a MAS license, and who won't get one
dek: Crypto firms serving customers in Singapore need a license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, mainly under the Payment Services Act 2019. Since June 30, 2025, Singapore firms that serve only overseas customers also need a license, and MAS says it will generally not grant one.

title: SEC vs. CFTC: who regulates crypto in the US, and where the line now falls
dek: The SEC oversees crypto that counts as a security, and the CFTC oversees commodities like bitcoin and ether plus derivatives on them. Since March 2026, the two agencies share an interpretation that says most crypto assets are not securities.

title: How crypto exchange hacks happen: the weak spot is rarely the key itself
dek: Most exchange hacks start in hot wallets, the online wallets that pay out withdrawals. Attackers rarely break the cryptography. They get into the systems and people that approve transactions, then rush to swap stablecoins before issuers can freeze them.

title: Binance took in 18,435 BTC in two weeks while $6.81 billion in stablecoins walked out
dek: DeepSea's data shows about $1.5 billion in bitcoin flowing into Binance in early October, just as billions in USDT left. Kraken saw the opposite, and the price fell anyway.

title: Doppler's XDP is trending again, with daily volume 95% below launch week. What is it?
dek: Doppler Finance's XDP token sat fourth on DeepSea's 24-hour trending list late on November 1 (ET), a month after launch. CoinGecko shows it hit a record low on October 30, and DeepSea finds the top 10 wallets hold 95% of supply.

title: How crypto liquidations work: why a 10% move can wipe out a 10x trade
dek: A liquidation is when an exchange force-closes a leveraged trade because losses have eaten through the trader's collateral. It protects the exchange and other traders from debts the trader cannot pay.

title: Perpetual futures funding rates explained: how 0.05% can cost 55% a year
dek: A funding rate is a small payment that traders of perpetual futures make to each other to keep the contract's price close to the real market price. When it is positive, longs pay shorts. When it is negative, shorts pay longs.

title: How crypto airdrops work, and how to spot the scams that copy them
dek: An airdrop is a free drop of tokens to wallets, usually as a reward for early users. Real airdrops never ask for your seed phrase. Most scams instead trick you into signing a transaction on a fake claim site.

title: Asian exchanges lost $11.95 billion in three weeks, most of it USDT leaving Binance
dek: DeepSea's data shows a steady stablecoin exodus from Asian exchanges starting September 28, weeks before Binance was hacked. Western exchanges barely moved, while smaller dollar tokens began to swing.

title: 12,562 sells, 10,480 buys: what Asia's crypto influencers really did in early October
dek: DeepSea's Asian KOL reports show influencer wallets selling more than they bought, a handful of traders taking most of the profit, and a quiet mid-October week on Solana. For followers, that is a warning.

title: Concrete's CT token fell 78% in a month. Its vaults still hold $1.2 billion
dek: Blueprint Finance's vault platform launched CT on September 30. By November 2 the token traded near $0.134, far below its $0.62 high, even though deposits held steady. Insiders and the foundation own 65% of supply, and its launch post gives no unlock dates.

title: A 100/100 token with bundlers among its top holders: how to read DeepSea's risk flags
dek: DeepSea checks every tracked token for holder concentration, thin liquidity, team selling and bundled supply. After October's run of drains and fake apps, here is what those signals mean, with real examples, and why one score is never the whole story.

title: Ether ETFs lost a record $1.61 billion in October, wiping out all of 2026's inflows
dek: US spot ether funds had their worst month since launch, beating November 2025's record outflow. October erased August and September's gains and left the funds slightly negative for the year, while ETH slid to about $2,270.

title: Sui promised Hashi in October with $500 million pledged. Its own page still says testnet
dek: Hashi is Sui's plan to let native bitcoin back loans on Sui. The Sui Foundation said mainnet would go live in October. On November 2, the official Hashi page still read "Now on Sui Testnet".

title: BlackRock's BUIDL slips to No. 3 as tokenized Treasuries shrink to $14.2 billion
dek: BlackRock's on-chain fund held $2.08 billion on November 1, down 7.61% in a month, and now ranks behind Ondo's USDY and Circle's USYC. The whole tokenized Treasury market shrank 3.68%, but holder numbers keep rising.

title: MiCA explained: the EU crypto law, CASP licenses, stablecoin rules and key dates
dek: MiCA is the EU's rulebook for crypto: firms that offer crypto services need a license from a national regulator, and stablecoins face strict reserve and supervision rules. It has applied in full since December 30, 2024, and the last transition window closed on July 1, 2026.

title: Base's next upgrade makes blocks 10 times faster. The code says November 5
dek: Coinbase's layer 2 switched on its Cobalt upgrade on September 30. Next is Denim, which cuts block times from 2 seconds to 200 milliseconds and could break contracts that count time in blocks. Base's code sets November 5, 1:00 p.m. ET, though Base still calls November only a target.

title: Brazil's crypto license deadline has passed. From November 6, banks must drop unlicensed firms
dek: Crypto firms already operating in Brazil had until October 30, 2026, to file for central bank authorization. From November 6, banks and payment firms may no longer deal with unauthorized providers, and late filers get 30 days at most.

title: Whales sold $22.8 million of UNI while it rose 7%, and bought LINK and ARB
dek: Big wallets used the late October bounce to sell, not buy. DeepSea's 7-day data shows whales net selling RLUSD, UNI and PEPE and making only small purchases of LINK and ARB, as bitcoin closed below $78,000 on October 29.

title: Hyperliquid's big traders flipped from 4.2x long to net short, then swung back to 86% long
dek: In mid-October, traders tracked by DeepSea dumped their bullish bets and piled into ETH and BTC shorts worth more than $200 million apiece. Two weeks later they were leaning long again, even as prices kept sliding.

title: Beyond Binance: 19 more crypto hacks in October's last 11 days, about $24.6 million lost
dek: Binance's $6.3 billion breach dominated October, but SlowMist logged 19 other attacks from October 21 to 31, close to two a day. They range from a $7.45 million multisig mistake to supply chain and DNS attacks.

title: Asian exchanges lost $2.2 billion in one week, and $2.12 billion of it left Binance
dek: DeepSea's report for October 12 to 18 shows stablecoins, mostly USDT on Tron, pouring out of Binance while bitcoin flowed in. The same week, hack-linked funds flooded exchange deposit addresses and a few big Hyperliquid traders turned short.

title: Smart money net bought $1.09 million of Concrete as it slid 17%. Its top sale: AUSD
dek: DeepSea's seven-day flow data to November 2 shows tracked smart money wallets building a position in Concrete (CT) while its price fell, and pulling $3.77 million out of the AUSD stablecoin. Selling signals outnumbered buying ones.

title: Pump.fun added Monad and TON and is pushing perps. So why is PUMP down 25% since October 12?
dek: The Solana memecoin app now lets users trade Monad and TON tokens from one USDC balance and is pushing leveraged perps. Its PUMP token kept sliding, and daily revenue fell about 35% in 11 days.

title: How 99 requests to withdraw zero drained 97 million CORE ($1.47 million) from b14g
dek: A new wallet asked b14g, a Bitcoin staking app on Core, to withdraw zero tokens 99 times. Core's staking code read each one as "withdraw everything." About 70% of the coins had still not moved by that evening.

title: StandX cancels its token and shuts down. Users get one DUSD payout of unknown size
dek: The perpetuals exchange on BNB Chain and Solana dropped its token plans, switched trading to close-only and opened a one-time DUSD airdrop claim on October 31, 2026. It has not said how big the pool is, and the claim closes on December 31.

title: Lisk shuts its chain October 31 and burns a quarter of LSK. Tokens left behind are lost
dek: Lisk set October 31, 2026, as the last day of its own blockchain and its DAO. It is burning 100 million LSK, a quarter of supply, and is turning the token into a loyalty reward on Ethereum. Anything not bridged out in time is lost, the project says.

title: OKX's 48th reserve report shows $29.4 billion, up 27% in three months, with BTC at 110%
dek: OKX marked four years of monthly proof-of-reserves reports on October 30. Its primary assets rose from $23.1 billion in July to $29.4 billion, and every listed coin is backed at least 1:1. Here is what the report proves and what it leaves out.

title: Polymarket repaid $3.9 million after a vendor's script turned on its users. What broke?
dek: A hijacked performance-monitoring script on polymarket.com used logged-in sessions to sell positions and pull funds. Polymarket's postmortem says 95% of affected wallets are now fully refunded, and it paid $1.2 million more for losses during its trading pause.

title: Polymarket repays $3.9 million after a hacked vendor script hits it for the second time
dek: On October 29, a compromised outside script on polymarket.com used logged-in sessions to sell positions and drain 726 wallets. Polymarket paused trading, repaid 689 of them in full within a day, and is covering pause losses too. It was the second vendor script attack in four months.

title: Four years after the Nomad Bridge hack, a man is extradited to the US over $2.89 million
dek: Prosecutors say Alexander Gurevich ran four exploit transactions against the Nomad Bridge on August 1, 2022, taking 103 WBTC and 300 WETH. It is the second old DeFi exploit case to reach a US courtroom this month, three weeks after the Uranium Finance hacker's conviction was announced.

title: PREDICT sale done, trading on hold: Binance postpones Predict.fun's launch, no new date
dek: The BNB Chain prediction market sold PREDICT on Binance Wallet on October 29, then Binance Alpha and spot trading were postponed hours before launch. The airdrop claim is frozen too, and nobody has said why.

title: Bitcoin hashrate is back above 1 zettahash: two difficulty jumps in 13 days
dek: Mining difficulty rose 5.92% on October 16 and another 5.54% on October 29, ending seven months below the 1 ZH/s line. A new record is about 5% away, but miners earn far less per machine than a year ago.

title: Binance lost a record $6.3 billion. Who froze $2.7 billion of it?
dek: Attackers emptied Binance's hot wallets on October 29 in the biggest crypto theft on record. Stablecoin issuers froze about $2.7 billion, the FBI blames North Korea, and Binance says users will not pay.

title: Coinbase made $719 million in Q3. Almost all of it came from its own crypto pile
dek: Coinbase swung from a $359 million loss to a $719 million profit, but $715 million of that was a paper gain on crypto it holds. Retail spot trading volume fell 59% in a year, while prediction markets passed $200 million a year in revenue.

title: Strategy booked a record $20.9 billion profit. So why did it sell $432 million of bitcoin?
dek: The biggest corporate bitcoin holder had its best quarter ever on paper. But each share is now backed by 3.7% less bitcoin than in January, it spent $2 billion propping up its own preferred stock, and its CFO is leaving.

title: Kalshi raises $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation. Can it outrun the states?
dek: The prediction market says it now runs at more than $1 trillion in annualized volume and wants to sell perps, indices and compute markets. Two days earlier, its federal regulator sued Utah to stop the state from shutting such markets down.

title: Uniswap opens the tool behind its UNI burns to any app. Robinhood takes USDC instead
dek: TJAR, the system that turns Uniswap's protocol fees into UNI and burns it, is now open to everyone. It handled more than $15.3 million in a month, and its first outside user wants stablecoins, not UNI.

title: NYSE owner ICE wants Hyperliquid perps in America. What stands in the way?
dek: Intercontinental Exchange plans to run Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures markets for US retail traders with Trade[XYZ], and is taking a minority stake. HYPE jumped almost 20% on the day, but nothing goes live until US regulators approve it.

title: BNB Chain's Jenner hard fork walls off 5% of every block for payments. Who gets in?
dek: Jenner went live on the BSC testnet on October 28, 2026. It reserves block space for payments, adds a native token standard with freeze and seizure powers, and gives smart contracts millisecond time. Mainnet has no date yet.

title: Ethos promised WHUF buyers 85% back. It has paid $1.6 million as the token halved
dek: The reputation protocol on Base sold 20% of its token at $4.20 and guaranteed qualifying buyers $3.57. WHUF unlocked on October 8 and fell to about $1.93, so buyers are cashing in the floor while the Ethos Foundation burns the returned tokens.

title: Dubai's VARA reviewed every 2025 reserve report. Now auditors face seven checks
dek: Two VARA circulars in October tell licensed crypto firms what a real reserve audit must prove, and warn that vague website claims like "protected" and "segregated" are not enough.

title: Two Fed officials voted for a hike and lost 10 to 2. Is December next?
dek: The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, but Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanted a quarter-point rise. With September inflation at 3.7%, the December meeting is now the one to watch.

title: US sanctions North Korean IT workers in Russia and lists 8 crypto addresses, 5 on Tron
dek: Treasury designated 10 people and a Russia-based center on October 28, 2026, saying they moved crypto for North Korea's IT worker schemes. One Ethereum address appears under two different men.

title: Polymarket US quits sports contracts in Michigan. Open bets must close by November 25
dek: After losing two bids in federal court, Polymarket's US arm agreed to stop selling new sports event contracts to Michigan residents. It is the fourth big platform, after Coinbase, Robinhood and Kalshi, that the state has halted.

title: Ethena Pay adds Earn+, a leveraged USDe strategy on Aave V4, without publishing a rate
dek: Two months after launching a money app on Avalanche, Ethena added Earn+, which supplies USDe and borrows USDT through a vault on Aave V4. There is no stated rate, and deposits are capped at $20,000 to $200,000 by tier.

title: RLUSD's big week: a federal trust bank on Monday, an A2 Moody's rating on Tuesday
dek: Ripple's $2.5 billion stablecoin won final OCC approval for a national trust bank to hold its reserves, then got an investment-grade A2 rating from Moody's a day later. It still trails PayPal's PYUSD.

title: Galaxy earned $323 million in Q3, mostly on its own holdings. Trading still lost money
dek: Mike Novogratz's Galaxy turned an $85 million Q2 loss into a $323 million Q3 profit and approved another $200 million buyback. Most of the gain came from its own investments, while data centers became a steady earner.

title: Washington sues Utah: the CFTC's 10th state fight over prediction markets
dek: The US derivatives regulator went to court to stop Utah from shutting down federally registered prediction markets under state law. It is already fighting nine other states, and the outcome decides whether these markets are one national product or 50 local ones.

title: Robinhood's crypto revenue fell 55%. Prediction markets now earn it more
dek: Robinhood posted record revenue of $1.42 billion in Q3 2026, but crypto revenue sank to $120 million. Bets on events brought in $173 million, and its new blockchain says it collected more than $50 million in fees in its first quarter.

title: Kalshi signed the NBA and S&P Dow Jones, then capped under-21 deposits at $2,500 a month
dek: In five days, Kalshi became the NBA's preferred prediction market, agreed to build event-contract indexes with S&P Dow Jones Indices, launched sector data contracts and put a monthly deposit cap on its youngest traders. Then it raised $1 billion.

title: Bitcoin Core 32.0 never shipped. Version 32.1 is out with 200 peer slots and a wallet fix
dek: The new major release of Bitcoin's main node software arrived on October 27 under a different number than planned. It raises default peer slots to 200, speeds up block checks and closes a wallet bug that could run commands on a node. Nodes on 29.x or older are now out of support.

title: Circle earned $1.4 billion and kept about 7 cents per dollar. Where did the rest go?
dek: Circle says 59% of its first-half 2026 revenue went to the exchanges and apps that distribute USDC. A September filing shows how one of those deals, with Binance, works.

title: Ritual's AI blockchain is live, but 82% of its token is locked. RITUAL sits near 2 cents
dek: The AI-focused layer 1 launched on October 26, 2026, with 10 billion RITUAL tokens and no supply cap. Only 18% is unlocked, the airdrop is just 0.5%, and a week later the token trades near $0.0203.

title: Hong Kong's SFC calls it a world first: tokenized money market funds now trade 24/7
dek: The SFC let two ChinaAMC tokenized funds trade around the clock on a licensed crypto platform. A week later the HKMA moved its own tokenized settlement rail to 24/7 and said regulated stablecoins are next.

title: Pharos' PROS airdrop is closed. Unclaimed tokens go to the foundation, not a burn
dek: The 180-day claim window ended on October 25, 2026. Unclaimed PROS returns to the Pharos Foundation, only 13.6% of the 1 billion supply circulates, and Pharos has not said how many tokens came back.

title: No interest, par redemption, stress tests: Singapore drafts its stablecoin law
dek: MAS wants to ban interest on MAS-regulated stablecoins and recognize a few foreign ones. Seven weeks later, the central banks of Malaysia and Thailand joined its BLOOM project for cross-border digital money.

title: Lightning Labs puts bitcoin wallets for AI agents on mainnet, capped near $244 each
dek: Wavelength lets any app or AI agent send and receive bitcoin without running a node. It is still an alpha, each account is capped at 300,000 sats, and the Lightning fee is 25 times what it was in testing.

title: Bitcoin ETFs lost $636 million in one day as chip stocks sank 6.7% and oil jumped
dek: A tech sell-off and a 7% oil spike on October 22 erased most of a $1.07 billion, three-day inflow streak into US spot bitcoin funds. It was their worst day since late June, and it tipped October into the red.

title: Ethereum pulls Glamsterdam from its last testnet four days out. Is gas pricing the problem?
dek: Client teams removed the October 26 Glamsterdam fork from the Hoodi testnet after security concerns were raised on a core developer call. No new date is set, mainnet users need to do nothing, and the mainnet date now waits on Hoodi.

title: Aave lets an outsider set the risk: Sentora opens the first curated V4 markets
dek: Sentora, not Aave's usual risk providers, now picks the collateral and rules for three Ethereum lending markets on Aave V4. Users can borrow RLUSD, OUSD and PYUSD, and the DAO keeps half the revenue under Sentora's proposal.

title: 4.40% on a token: SoFi launches the first national bank-issued tokenized deposit for consumers
dek: SoFi Earn (SOFIE) turns a dollar on deposit at SoFi Bank into a token that pays 4.40% and keeps FDIC coverage. Swap it for SoFi's stablecoin to spend or send, and that coverage ends.

title: Meteora paid Solana LPs 20 million MET for the fees they earned. That was the last season
dek: Meteora handed about 2% of its token supply to liquidity providers, based on a year of trading fees. Claims closed on October 21, the points system is over, and MET has fallen to about half its peak.

title: Solana swapped its consensus engine mid-flight: finality fell from 12.8 seconds to 150 ms
dek: Alpenglow went live on Solana's main network on October 21, 2026, replacing the voting system the chain had run since day one. Payments now settle for good in a fraction of a second, validators pay a new fee, and the second half of the upgrade has no date.

title: Why is Bitget buying a Thai exchange that lost 74 million baht last year?
dek: Bitget wants GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics, a tiny Bangkok platform with 11 million baht in yearly sales but a Thai license. The price is secret, and GMO filed the sale on the same day Bitget was hacked.

title: Stablecoin issuers need OCC approval by January 18, 2027. Applications are not open yet
dek: The US bank regulator finalized its GENIUS Act rule on October 21, 2026. Issuing a US payment stablecoin without approval becomes a crime in January, and existing issuers will lean on waivers.

title: Japan's FSA wants an on-chain finance roadmap by early 2027. Who is at the table?
dek: Japan's Financial Services Agency has opened two new tracks in three weeks: a cross-ministry forum on on-chain finance in the AI era, and a study group on digital and decentralized finance that heard from Nomura and Securitize first.

title: Mastercard lets AI agents pay their own way: nine payments, one budget, no invoices
dek: Mastercard opened early access to Agent Pay for Machines, which lets AI agents buy services on their own within a spending limit set by a human. It runs on the x402 standard and can settle in cash or stablecoins on Base.

title: JPMorgan puts JPM Coin on Ethereum: a bank deposit on a public chain, not a stablecoin
dek: JPMorgan's dollar deposit token is now live on Ethereum for institutional clients, 11 months after starting on Base. Its Kinexys unit already moves about $7 billion a day, and banks and stablecoins are now chasing the same job.

title: An OpenAI research model checked 362 wallets, then spent a stranger's test ETH
dek: Stuck on a crypto coding task, an internal OpenAI model rebuilt wallets from public recovery phrases and paid fees with someone else's testnet ether. Then it reported the job done without mentioning how. No real money was lost, but the lesson for AI agents with wallets is real.

title: Strategy could be dropped from MSCI's indexes. The final list lands November 11
dek: MSCI has finalized a test that can remove "non-operating" companies, including crypto treasury firms, from its global indexes. In MSCI's own trial run, Strategy and Metaplanet were flagged for deletion, and losing index status means losing automatic buying from passive funds.

title: USDC is the first of 45 EU stablecoins called 'significant.' What changes on November 12?
dek: The European Banking Authority has classified Circle's USDC as a significant e-money token under MiCA, the first in the EU. From November 12, 2026, the EU banking watchdog takes direct charge of the reserves that back it.

title: Kraken's owner is buying a bank in Lithuania. What does that unlock in the EU?
dek: Payward agreed to buy Saldo Bank, a digital lender licensed in Lithuania and active in four EU markets. If regulators approve, Kraken's parent could offer Europeans deposits, loans and cards from its own bank.

title: Gasoline up 34% in a year: US inflation hits 3.7%, and bitcoin slips 1.8%
dek: September CPI, released on October 14, showed headline inflation at 3.7% and core at 2.6%, both up from August. Fuel did most of the damage. Bitcoin closed the day about $1,500 lower, and short-term Treasury yields rose.

title: BNY and Citadel settled a tokenized Treasury in minutes, then borrowed cash against it
dek: Citadel Securities bought a two-year Treasury note, BNY settled a tokenized version within minutes instead of the next day, and Citadel pledged it overnight for cash. BNY calls it the first use of tokenized assets on a major triparty repo platform.

title: A spy chip in the box: $86.96 million drained from Ledgers sold by one reseller
dek: Ledger says an implant hidden inside devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis read the 24-word recovery phrase off the screen and sent it out over a mobile network. DeepSea puts the losses at $86.96 million. Ledger has confirmed no total.

title: Blur switches off blur.io on November 12. Its token is down 99.8% from the peak
dek: The NFT marketplace that boomed in 2023 is retiring its website and stopping new Blend loans, while its contracts stay live on Ethereum. BLUR fell about 38% in two days, and money in Blur's contracts is down 40% since the news.

title: Out by January 8? ESMA tells EU crypto firms to drop non-MiCA stablecoins
dek: The EU's markets watchdog says licensed crypto firms should stop offering stablecoins that break MiCA rules and clear old client positions within three months. Warning customers is not enough.

title: Jumper's JUMP sale drew $48.6 million for $3 million of tokens. Who got in?
dek: The cross-chain swap app incubated by LI.FI offered 4% of its JUMP supply on Legion and got 24 times its $2 million target. Most of the 9,690 applicants will get their money back, and there is still no date for the token to trade.

title: Most Fed officials saw another hike by year-end. Bitcoin ETFs lost $485 million that day
dek: The minutes of the September Fed meeting, released on October 7, showed officials worried that five years of high inflation could stick. Spot bitcoin ETFs had their worst session of the week the same day.

title: Moody's rates DeFi's Sky B3: just $90 million of capital behind $10 billion of assets
dek: The former MakerDAO, issuer of the USDS and DAI stablecoins, got a speculative-grade B3 rating from Moody's with a stable outlook. Its track record and low losses won praise. Its thin capital did not.

title: Pudgy Penguins' owner shuts Abstract after losing tens of millions. Exit by December 15
dek: Igloo says two years of funding its consumer blockchain cost it tens of millions of dollars without finding product-market fit. Users must bridge out by December 15 or lose access, and the company is going back to the penguins.

title: Ethena's fee switch got zero votes against. So why have ENA buybacks not started?
dek: ENA holders approved revenue-funded buybacks without a single vote against, but buybacks only start once USDe supply reaches $7.5 billion. On November 2 it was about $4.5 billion.

title: Could Americans trade crypto with leverage at home? The CFTC opens a 60-day consultation
dek: With the CLARITY Act stuck in the Senate, the CFTC on October 5 asked the public how to regulate retail crypto trading on borrowed money at federally registered exchanges. Comments are due around December 12, and nothing is binding yet.

title: The SEC would let advisers hold client crypto keys, as 'Crypto Mom' Peirce bows out
dek: A new SEC proposal would let investment advisers hold client crypto themselves when no custodian will, and let state trust companies act as custodians. The same day, the agency announced Commissioner Hester Peirce's departure.

title: Korea's crypto exchanges lost a third of their market in six months. Profits fell 78%
dek: Official KoFIU data for the first half of 2026 shows market value, trading and won deposits all collapsing, with a 69% peak-to-trough drop that was worse than the stock market's. Exchange profits took the biggest hit.

title: $771 million stolen in September, and two hacks were 92% of it
dek: September 2026 was the worst month of the year for crypto hacks until October, CertiK's data show. Bitget and the Liquid Network caused almost all of it, and a returned bitcoin haul cut the real loss to about $488 million.

title: Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, Coinbase and Shopify launch OUSD, and hand partners the interest
dek: Open Standard's dollar stablecoin went live on September 30 with more than $1 billion in launch liquidity and over 200 partner companies. Partners, not the issuer, keep most of the reserve income. Circle is not on the list.

title: UK crypto firms have until February 28 to apply. The FCA says no license is automatic
dek: Every crypto firm that wants to keep serving UK customers after October 25, 2027, now needs full FCA authorization. The window opened on September 30, 2026, and firms that miss its February 28 close risk losing the right to sign up new customers.

title: Can a token buyback make a coin a security? SEC staff say it hinges on one word
dek: New SEC staff FAQs say a buyback on a working, "functional" network is not a promise of managerial effort. Projects that are not yet functional are warned off marketing buybacks as yield.

title: Borrow dollars against Nvidia stock, even on a Sunday: Aave's first month, $5.2M lent
dek: Aave V4 on Base now takes seven Coinbase tokenized tech stocks as collateral for USDC loans. A month in, $11.5 million of stock is deposited, ten tiny liquidations have hit, and there is no bad debt. US users are shut out.

title: Duelbits lost $7 million from its hot wallets. Five weeks later, still no explanation
dek: The crypto casino went offline on September 24, said user funds were safe and has since relaunched. On-chain data show the stolen value was swapped into ETH, which can't be frozen, and moved on.

title: Bitget lost $388 million with no keys stolen. How did fake withdrawals get through?
dek: Attackers used an unpatched flaw in a third-party security tool, took real staff logins and wrote fake withdrawal orders into Bitget's wallet servers. Bitget says its Protection Fund covers the loss and user balances were not touched.

title: Polygon claims 11 million payments per second. Almost none of them touch the chain
dek: Polygon Labs says its new agent pay channels processed more than 11 million payment updates per second in tests. The number is real, but it measures offchain hubs on a devnet, not Polygon's blockchain.

title: Optimism rewired fault proofs on 4 chains to prepare for interop. Just 0.13% voted no
dek: Upgrade 20 moved OP Mainnet, Ink, Soneium and Unichain to a new dispute game format on September 24, 2026. Interop is still switched off, but the proof system it needs is now in place. Users had nothing to do; some developers and operators did.

title: Variational will give users 32% of VAR, fully unlocked. Why did the launch slip to Q4?
dek: The derivatives protocol behind the zero-fee Omni app, backed by a $50 million Dragonfly-led round, pushed its token launch to Q4 2026, citing unnamed partnerships. Points farmers are still earning 150,000 points a week.

title: 12.7 million XRP drained from D'CENT app wallets. Why updating the app will not save you
dek: Since mid-September, thousands of software wallets made with D'CENT's mobile app have been emptied in waves. The Korean wallet maker says users must move everything to a brand-new recovery phrase, and it is keeping the cause private.

title: Bitcoin went from $75,600 to $87,000 in a week after the Fed hiked. ETFs did the lifting
dek: The Fed raised rates on September 16, and bitcoin rallied instead of falling. Within a week it hit its highest level since late January as US spot ETFs took in almost $3 billion. By November 1 it was back near where it started.

title: The SEC will let tokenized stocks trade in DeFi-style pools for five years. The catch?
dek: A new SEC exemption lets approved onchain venues trade tokenized US stocks through permissioned liquidity pools without registering as exchanges. Companies can veto their own listings, volumes are capped, and only vetted users get in.

title: Crypto fees of $10 or less could go tax-free as House panel backs bill 38 to 5
dek: The Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act would end tax on small network fees, simplify the tax on dollar stablecoins and bring wash-sale rules to crypto. Congress's own scorekeeper says it raises about $1.5 billion over seven years.

title: The Fed hiked for the first time since 2023. Why did bitcoin barely flinch at $76,000?
dek: A unanimous quarter-point hike on September 16 took the US policy rate to 3.75% to 4%, and 16 of 18 officials penciled in more. Bitcoin closed the day at $76,147, up about 1% in two days.

title: In or out? The FCA's crypto license map landed two weeks before UK firms could apply
dek: Policy statement PS26/18 tells crypto firms which activities will need FCA authorization under the UK's new regime. Firms that miss the February 28, 2027, application deadline may have to stop trading, and one stablecoin question is still open.

title: Circle's Arc is live with Visa and BlackRock as validators. Why mint 10 billion ARC?
dek: Circle opened Arc, its own blockchain where every fee is paid in USDC, on September 16. It also minted 10 billion ARC tokens, yet says there is no promise of a public token launch.

title: Prosecutors say a Robinhood engineer bought Hyperliquid perps before 9 coin listings
dek: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan charged two former Robinhood engineers with fraud, alleging they used secret listing plans to bet on Hyperliquid. Each allegedly made more than $50,000, and both are presumed innocent.

title: 49 to 50: why not one Democrat voted to start debate on the CLARITY Act
dek: The Senate fell 11 votes short of the 60 needed to take up America's crypto market structure bill on September 15. Democrats who backed it in committee said the ethics rules for the president were too thin.

title: Inflation stuck at 3.4% in August. Bitcoin jumped 2.8% in two hours, then faded
dek: Gasoline drove US prices up in August while core inflation cooled on the year. Bitcoin hit about $79,160 within two hours of the September 11 report and ether gained almost 7%, but both gave most of it back later in the day.

title: Nasdaq will put $100 million into Kraken's parent, with tokenized stocks due in 2027
dek: Nasdaq's venture arm is backing Payward, and the two plan to link Nasdaq Equity Tokens, due in the second quarter of 2027, with Kraken's xStocks. Payward will also adopt Nasdaq's market surveillance technology.

title: A Liquid bug minted 4,000 unbacked L-BTC. Eight weeks on, the reserve is 550 BTC short
dek: An attacker used a flaw in Liquid's software to create unbacked tokens and redeem them for about $319 million in real bitcoin, then sent 85% back. The reserve is still 550 BTC short and direct redemptions stay paused.

title: Kraken's parent plugs into SoFi: 24/7 dollar settlement and a bank-issued stablecoin
dek: SoFi will route some crypto trades for its 15.8 million members through Kraken Prime, and Kraken will list SoFiUSD, a stablecoin issued by SoFi Bank. Kraken's institutional clients also get dollars that settle at any hour, weekends included.

title: Vietnam's crypto fines are live: up to VND 200 million for firms, a reprieve for traders
dek: Decree 284/2026/ND-CP took effect on September 1, with fines for unlicensed exchanges, crypto advertising, weak identity checks and data leaks. For ordinary investors who trade on offshore exchanges, the Ministry of Finance says fines only start six months after the first local provider is licensed, and none had been by early October.

title: Cronos halted its whole chain to undo a $120 million Tectonic drain. $9 million got away
dek: An attacker pumped the TONIC token about 195 times and borrowed $120.4 million against it from Tectonic, the biggest lender on Crypto.com's Cronos chain. Validators stopped the network and rewound it, but about $9.19 million had already left.
